#+title: Build and Cache

* Agreed Workflow
- Personal edits: test locally, commit as often as needed, then push the completed changes to =main=.
  A push starts preparation, without upgrading inputs. A clean snapshot proceeds to builds; a
  corrected Caddy hash becomes a repair PR instead of silently changing main or building stale input.
- Dependency automation: create an update PR with Nix's lock-file change log; approve its cache jobs,
  review the build results, then merge manually. Richer reports are planned. Merging starts a build
  of the final =main= commit.
- Same derivations reuse cached outputs. Different source snapshots or metadata can still require
  small generated outputs to be rebuilt; two workflow runs do not imply recompiling every package.
- Upgrade manually after the main-branch cache job completes. An urgent local input update or switch
  is always allowed; missing outputs can still build locally. Local builds are not automatically
  uploaded to Cachix.

* Current Implementation
[[file:workflows/update.yml][Prepare configuration]] owns main-branch pushes, schedules, and manual dispatches. On pushes it
checks the exact pushed snapshot without running =nix flake update=. If no hash correction is
needed, it calls [[file:workflows/build.yml][Build and cache]] as a reusable workflow for that same commit. If a correction is
needed, it creates/updates =automation/caddy-hash= and skips building the uncorrected main snapshot.
The repair PR triggers the normal PR build, subject to approval; merging remains manual.

The build workflow also handles PRs targeting =main= directly. It does not independently listen to
main pushes, so preparation and builds cannot race. Ordinary branch pushes, fork PRs, and manual
runs on other branches are skipped. There are still only two workflow files.

| Runner       | Platform       | System outputs |
|--------------+----------------+----------------|
| ubuntu-24.04 | x86_64-linux   | az, echo, hws  |
| macos-15     | aarch64-darwin | rhayader       |

Linux targets share one Nix store. A failed build skips the explicit final upload for that job;
Cachix may already have uploaded successfully built dependencies. The other platform continues.
The final upload is a separate step: a successful build alone does not mean the cache is ready.
All Actions are pinned to commit SHAs.

** CI Cache Sources
| Cache                      | Purpose / evidence                                      |
|----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| cache.nixos.org            | Default official Nixpkgs cache; retained by the installer |
| cache.numtide.com          | llm-agents' documented binary cache                      |
| cache.thalheim.io          | Declared by sops-nix's flake and used in its CI           |
| feel-co.cachix.org         | Public cache used by Hjem's documentation CI              |
| nix-community.cachix.org   | Swift build dependencies absent from the official cache  |
| CACHIX_CACHE               | This repository's own outputs and runtime closures       |

Addresses and explicit keys were checked against the currently locked inputs; =feel-co='s public
key was also checked with the Cachix API. Cachix configures that cache and key through =extraPullNames=.
Hjem's documentation CI is evidence of upstream use, not a guarantee that our runtime outputs hit
that cache. =nix-index-database= downloads its pre-generated database from a pinned GitHub release;
it does not require adding =nix-community.cachix.org= for that download. No dedicated cache is added
for nix-darwin, and no unrelated CUDA, editor, or desktop caches are enabled.

The =nix-community= cache is not synonymous with NUR. The first Darwin CI run compiled Swift
dependencies for =age-plugin-se= that were absent from the official cache but available from
=nix-community=; the local Mac's matching Swift outputs also carried its signatures. Keep it in CI
to avoid that cold build. An upstream cache hit depends on the exact output, platform, and
dependencies. Missing outputs can still build and enter the personal cache.

Clients should keep at least the official cache and =suspen.cachix.org=: Cachix normally skips
uploading paths already available from =cache.nixos.org=. Third-party paths needed by a successfully
uploaded system closure can be served by the personal cache, subject to retention and availability.
This does not guarantee caching every build-time-only dependency. Host cache settings are separate
and unchanged here.

* GitHub Setup: Required Before Enabling Uploads
1. Create a Cachix cache and a write token scoped to that cache. Choose its visibility deliberately:
   anyone who can read the cache can inspect uploaded store contents, including generated configs.
   The official and community caches remain upstreams; this is not a mirror of all Nixpkgs.
2. In repository Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables, set =CACHIX_CACHE= to
   the cache name (not its URL).
3. In Settings -> Environments, create both environments below *before* running the workflow.
   Put =CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN= in each environment's secrets, not in repository or organization secrets.

| Environment    | Required protection                                     |
|----------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| nix-cache-main | Selected branches/tags: allow only the branch =main=     |
| nix-cache-pr   | Required reviewers: yourself; review each candidate run |

For =nix-cache-pr=, leave "Prevent self-review" disabled so the sole maintainer can approve their
own runs. Restrict its allowed branches to =refs/pull/*/merge= if using selected-branch rules.
Approval permits the candidate code to run with the cache write credential: review workflow and
build-code changes before approving. Same-repository origin alone does not establish trust.

GitHub applies Environment protection before jobs start and releases secrets only after approval.
The workflow cannot configure those protections itself. Do not enable PR uploads if required
reviewers are unavailable on your repository's GitHub plan/visibility; agree on a different gate
first. Keep cache credentials out of repository/organization secrets so candidate workflows cannot
obtain them without the corresponding Environment gate. Do not use =pull_request_target= to build
candidate code with write credentials.

4. Commit and push the workflow when ready. Once it is on =main=, it can also be run through
   Actions -> Prepare configuration -> Run workflow, selecting =main= and mode =check= to test the
   current lock without upgrading, or mode =update= to prepare dependency updates.
5. Check both platforms' build, final upload, and Cachix post-job steps. Fix failures and rerun the
   failed jobs as needed. No activation or deployment is performed by this workflow.

The Nix installer permits CI substitutions for =allowSubstitutes = false= derivations; local
substitution policy is unchanged. No production SOPS keys are needed. Only the committed snapshot
and its lock file are built; local uncommitted or untracked files are not sent to the runner.

* Dependency Update PRs
[[file:workflows/update.yml][Prepare configuration]] updates inputs weekly on Sunday at 03:00 UTC (11:00 Asia/Shanghai), or
manually on =main= in mode =update= (the manual default). Pushes and mode =check= never upgrade the
lock. Scheduled jobs can be delayed by GitHub. Preparation needs no Cachix write credentials; the
separate build jobs obtain those through their protected Environments.

The workflow calls [[file:scripts/update-inputs.py][update-inputs.py]] once. In update mode it records the recipe, updates the lock,
then compares and conditionally refreshes/verifies Caddy. On a push it compares against the previous
pushed commit, if available. Without a baseline (first push, rewritten history, or manual check),
it refreshes conservatively with =nix-update=. An unchanged push baseline is skipped only when its
Linux cache check succeeded; otherwise the hash is checked so a pre-existing failure is not ignored.
Reporting remains a separate step. The PR action's existing output decides what happens
next: a repair PR triggers candidate builds; no repair PR allows building the original snapshot.

- Empty =inputs=: update all inputs.
- Space-separated input names, e.g. =llm-agents= or =hjem darwin=: request updates to those inputs.
  Input handling is delegated to Nix. Indirect lock changes can still occur
  when an input's dependencies change or its references need reconciliation.
- Dependency changes create or update =automation/flake-update=; push/check hash repairs use the
  separate =automation/caddy-hash= branch so a repair does not replace a pending dependency update.
  No difference means no new PR is needed. =create-pull-request= manages the branch
  lifecycle and only stages =flake.lock= and =hosts/hws/default.nix=. Nix commits lock changes in
  the temporary runner checkout; the action includes that commit and any hash correction in the PR.
- Each run starts from the latest =main=; it does not accumulate pending updates from an earlier
  unmerged PR. Reserve the automation branch for the updater, not unrelated manual commits.
- The separate =FLAKE_UPDATE_TOKEN= repository secret must be a token restricted to this repository
  with Contents and Pull requests read/write permissions. Default =GITHUB_TOKEN= PR creation does
  not normally trigger another Actions workflow. No automatic merge or activation is configured.
- The first report contains Nix's input/revision/date change log and any Caddy hash change. Package
  versions, upstream comparison links, and selected-module effects are still a separate reporting step.
- The PR body reserves =<!-- update-report:start -->= / =<!-- update-report:end -->= for the future
  report writer. These are placeholders only; no report generation or LLM call runs yet.

After committing and pushing both workflows, a manual update can be requested with:
#+begin_src sh
gh workflow run update.yml --repo hejsu/flakes --ref main
# Or update only llm-agents:
gh workflow run update.yml --repo hejsu/flakes --ref main -f inputs=llm-agents
# Check/repair current main without upgrading any input:
gh workflow run update.yml --repo hejsu/flakes --ref main -f mode=check
# Recompute Caddy's hash even if its declared inputs are unchanged:
gh workflow run update.yml --repo hejsu/flakes --ref main -f mode=check -f refresh-caddy=true
#+end_src

Review and approve the resulting PR's =nix-cache-pr= jobs, then merge manually after reviewing the
results. The existing build workflow handles PR and post-merge caching. GitHub branch protection
is not configured here, so a failed job is visible but does not itself prohibit merging.

** Automatic Caddy Hash Refresh
The update script keeps the original recipe in memory and, only when needed, invokes =nix-update=
followed by source verification. It does not implement hash discovery, parse build errors, or edit
Nix files itself.

Compare hws's Caddy source =drvPath= against the baseline described above. This only evaluates the
derivation: it does not build or fetch the plugin dependencies. If the path is unchanged, skip
prefetching and verification. A changed derivation means its hash needs checking, not necessarily
that the hash will change. This detects changes to Go/build inputs too, unlike a version-only check.
Use the manual =refresh-caddy= input to bypass the skip when repairing an already stale hash or
rechecking external dependency drift that is not represented in the derivation. Evaluation errors
stop the update rather than being treated as "unchanged".

The cheap comparison detects changes, not arbitrary external dependency drift. A failed or missing
Linux check triggers a conservative hash refresh, without downloading old CI logs. Manual mode
=check= or the force option can also recheck the current hash. An unchanged recipe does not prove
the entire system is valid; complete builds still follow preparation.

When needed, use [[https://github.com/Mic92/nix-update][nix-update]] from the locked Nixpkgs input, not a custom hash-parsing script.
=--version=skip --src-only= refreshes only the source hash of hws's configured Caddy package.
=--override-filename= directs the edit to the host file rather than Nixpkgs' read-only store source.
The workflow then builds =package.src= with the new hash before creating the PR; failures stop the
update. Full Caddy compilation and plugin checks remain in =build.yml=.

The tool computes hashes with a placeholder build internally. It does not upgrade the plugin
version, automatically merge, or establish the safety of newly fetched dependencies. Hash diffs
appear in the PR alongside the lock changes. The same command works with a native or remote
x86_64-linux builder:
#+begin_src sh
nix run --no-update-lock-file --inputs-from . nixpkgs#nix-update -- \
  --flake --version=skip --src-only --system x86_64-linux \
  --override-filename hosts/hws/default.nix \
  nixosConfigurations.hws.config.services.caddy.package
#+end_src

Direct pushes to =main= are never rewritten. Preflight either passes the exact commit to the build
workflow, or publishes the hash fix as a PR and leaves main builds skipped until a corrected commit
is merged. A successful preparation alone is not a successful system build: check the called build
jobs or repair PR before upgrading. No automatic merge or deployment is enabled. A Mac without a
Linux builder cannot compute this Linux-specific source output locally.

** Future Report Layer
Keep reporting separate from updating and caching. After both platform jobs finish, a separately
scoped report job should update the reserved PR-body block on success or failure, provided the
candidate commit is still current. It must not require builds to succeed before explaining a
failure. LLM/API failures should leave the raw checks and logs available, not block cache uploads.
An edit pushed to the PR branch automatically triggers another build; retrying an unchanged run is
mainly useful for transient infrastructure failures. None of this reporting is implemented yet.

* Next Steps
- [ ] Configure client substituters/public keys, including Determinate Nix's =nix.custom.conf=,
  and verify a real cache download. Uploading alone does not enable local consumption.
- [X] Add weekly/manual dependency-update PRs, with optional input selection such as =llm-agents=.
- [ ] Add input/package/selected-module change reports, using separately scoped reporting permissions.
- [ ] Measure cache storage and download performance, then choose retention for recent systems.

Homebrew, runtime container images/subscriptions, production state, automatic merges, automatic
activation, extra VM/integration tests, and a separate release branch are outside this first step.
